title: Why can't we just print more money? 💸
description:
Ten apples, ten dollars, and a money printer: the simplest way to understand inflation, and what happened when Zimbabwe tried it.

Sources: Hanke & Kwok, Cato Journal (2009); Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe Z$100 trillion note, Jan 2009.

meta.overrides: style test v3: living town (faceless townspeople), depth staging, smoother stall/apples

speaker: ved

scenes.say: Hey! Ever wondered why a country can't just *print more money*?
Picture a tiny island. It has *ten apples*, and *ten dollars* in total.
Now the government prints ten more dollars, and hands them out.
Everyone feels richer! Twice the money...

scenes.say: So the seller raises the price. Each apple now costs *two dollars*. That's *inflation*.
Nobody got richer. Prices just went up.

beat.text:
The printer: "I'm the birthday."
Prices: *"Me too."*

scenes.say: Zimbabwe actually tried this. In 2008, prices *doubled* about every single day...
...and it printed a *one hundred trillion* dollar note.
See, money isn't wealth. It's a *ticket* for the stuff we make.
Print more tickets... and each one *buys less*.
